ജെൻഡർ പൊളിറ്റിക്സും ഇസ്ലാമിക ലോകവീക്ഷണവും: ഒരു സമഗ്ര വിശകലനം

സമകാലിക ലോകത്ത് ഏറെ ചർച്ച ചെയ്യപ്പെടുന്ന വിഷയമാണ് ജെൻഡർ പൊളിറ്റിക്സ് (Gender Politics). ഇൻസ്റ്റിറ്റ്യൂട്ട് ഫോർ ഇന്റലക്ച്വൽ ഡിസ്‌കോഴ്‌സിന് (Institute for Intellectual Discourse) വേണ്ടി ഡോ. നിസാമുദ്ദീൻ എം.പി അവതരിപ്പിച്ച ഈ വിഷയം, ആധുനിക പാശ്ചാത്യ ലോകവീക്ഷണവും (Modern Western Worldview) ഇസ്ലാമിക ലോകവീക്ഷണവും (Islamic Worldview) തമ്മിലുള്ള അടിസ്ഥാനപരമായ വ്യത്യാസങ്ങളെ ആഴത്തിൽ വിശകലനം ചെയ്യുന്നു.

പാശ്ചാത്യ ലിബറൽ ചിന്താഗതികൾ എങ്ങനെയാണ് ധാർമികത, കുടുംബം, ലൈംഗികത എന്നീ വിഷയങ്ങളെ മാറ്റിയെഴുതാൻ ശ്രമിക്കുന്നതെന്നും, അതിനെതിരെ ഇസ്ലാം മുന്നോട്ട് വെക്കുന്ന വ്യക്തമായ കാഴ്ചപ്പാടുകൾ എന്തൊക്കെയാണെന്നും ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ വിശദീകരിക്കുന്നു.

ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ ചർച്ച ചെയ്യുന്ന പ്രധാന കാര്യങ്ങൾ:

- ലോകവീക്ഷണങ്ങളിലെ സംഘർഷം: ദൈവികമായ അറിവുകൾ (Revelation) അടിസ്ഥാനമാക്കിയുള്ള ഇസ്ലാമിക കാഴ്ചപ്പാടും, ഭൗതികവാദത്തിൽ (Materialism) ഊന്നിയുള്ള ആധുനിക കാഴ്ചപ്പാടും തമ്മിലുള്ള വ്യത്യാസം.

- സെക്സും ജെൻഡറും: ജൈവശാസ്ത്രപരമായ ലിംഗഭേദവും (Biological Sex) സാമൂഹിക നിർമ്മിതിയായി വാദിക്കപ്പെടുന്ന ജെൻഡറും (Gender as a social construct) തമ്മിലുള്ള ആശയക്കുഴപ്പങ്ങൾ.

- ലൈംഗിക വിപ്ലവം (Sexual Revolution): 1960-കൾക്ക് ശേഷം പാശ്ചാത്യ ലോകത്തുണ്ടായ സാംസ്കാരിക മാറ്റങ്ങളും, അത് കുടുംബ സംവിധാനങ്ങളെ തകർത്ത രീതിയും.

- ഇസ്ലാമിക നിലപാട്: ആൺ-പെൺ ദ്വന്ദ്വം (Binary), സ്വവർഗ ലൈംഗികതയോടുള്ള സമീപനം, ഉഭയലിംഗം (Intersex) vs ട്രാൻസ്‌ജെൻഡർ, കുടുംബത്തിന്‍റെയും ധാർമികതയുടെയും പ്രാധാന്യം.

- പരിഹാരങ്ങൾ: ഈ ആശയക്കുഴപ്പങ്ങൾക്കിടയിൽ മുസ്ലിം സമൂഹം മുറുകെ പിടിക്കേണ്ട ആറ് മാർഗ്ഗനിർദ്ദേശങ്ങൾ.

title: 40 Hadiths of Imam Nawawi | Hadith #26 | ألأربعون النووي
description:
ഇമാം നവവിയുടെ 40 ഹദീസുകളുടെ വിവരണങ്ങളടങ്ങുന്ന സീരീസ്. 

ഹദീസ്‌ #26
|| ദൈവാനുഗ്രഹങ്ങളോടുള്ള കൃതജ്ഞത ||


عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم "كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنْ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ، كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ تَعْدِلُ بَيْنَ اثْنَيْنِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُعِينُ الرَّجُلَ فِي دَابَّتِهِ فَتَحْمِلُهُ عَلَيْهَا أَوْ تَرْفَعُ لَهُ عَلَيْهَا مَتَاعَهُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ، وَبِكُلِّ خُطْوَةٍ تَمْشِيهَا إلَى الصَّلَاةِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَتُمِيطُ الْأَذَى عَنْ الطَّرِيقِ صَدَقَةٌ".

title: 40 Hadiths of Imam Nawawi | Hadith #25 | ألأربعون النووي
description:
ഇമാം നവവിയുടെ 40 ഹദീസുകളുടെ വിവരണങ്ങളടങ്ങുന്ന സീരീസ്. 

ഹദീസ്‌ #25
|| സുകൃതങ്ങളുടെ അനന്തസാധ്യത ||

عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا، "أَنَّ نَاسًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم قَالُوا لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ذَهَبَ أَهْلُ الدُّثُورِ بِالْأُجُورِ؛ يُصَلُّونَ كَمَا نُصَلِّي، وَيَصُومُونَ كَمَا نَصُومُ، وَيَتَصَدَّقُونَ بِفُضُولِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ. قَالَ: أَوَلَيْسَ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ مَا تَصَّدَّقُونَ؟ إنَّ بِكُلِّ تَسْبِيحَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَكْبِيرَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَحْمِيدَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَكُلِّ تَهْلِيلَةٍ صَدَقَةً، وَأَمْرٌ بِمَعْرُوفٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَنَهْيٌ عَنْ مُنْكَرٍ صَدَقَةٌ، وَفِي بُضْعِ أَحَدِكُمْ صَدَقَةٌ. قَالُوا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيَأْتِي أَحَدُنَا شَهْوَتَهُ وَيَكُونُ لَهُ فِيهَا أَجْرٌ؟ قَالَ: أَرَأَيْتُمْ لَوْ وَضَعَهَا فِي حَرَامٍ أَكَانَ عَلَيْهِ وِزْرٌ؟ فَكَذَلِكَ إذَا وَضَعَهَا فِي الْحَلَالِ، كَانَ لَهُ أَجْرٌ". [رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ].

عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: "كُنْت خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم يَوْمًا، فَقَالَ: يَا غُلَامِ! إنِّي أُعَلِّمُك كَلِمَاتٍ: احْفَظْ اللَّهَ يَحْفَظْك، احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ تُجَاهَك، إذَا سَأَلْت فَاسْأَلْ اللَّهَ، وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْت فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاَللَّهِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْأُمَّةَ لَوْ اجْتَمَعَتْ عَلَى أَنْ يَنْفَعُوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَنْفَعُوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ لَك، وَإِنْ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى أَنْ يَضُرُّوك بِشَيْءٍ لَمْ يَضُرُّوك إلَّا بِشَيْءٍ قَدْ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْك؛ رُفِعَتْ الْأَقْلَامُ، وَجَفَّتْ الصُّحُفُ" . رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ [رقم:2516] وَقَالَ: حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ. وَفِي رِوَايَةِ غَيْرِ التِّرْمِذِيِّ: "احْفَظْ اللَّهَ تَجِدْهُ أمامك، تَعَرَّفْ إلَى اللَّهِ فِي الرَّخَاءِ يَعْرِفُك فِي الشِّدَّةِ، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَا أَخْطَأَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُصِيبَك، وَمَا أَصَابَك لَمْ يَكُنْ لِيُخْطِئَك، وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ النَّصْرَ مَعَ الصَّبْرِ، وَأَنْ الْفَرَجَ مَعَ الْكَرْبِ، وَأَنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا".

عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ أَيْضًا قَالَ: " بَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ جُلُوسٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ، إذْ طَلَعَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلٌ شَدِيدُ بَيَاضِ الثِّيَابِ، شَدِيدُ سَوَادِ الشَّعْرِ، لَا يُرَى عَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ السَّفَرِ، وَلَا يَعْرِفُهُ مِنَّا أَحَدٌ. حَتَّى جَلَسَ إلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه و سلم . فَأَسْنَدَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إلَى رُكْبَتَيْهِ، وَوَضَعَ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى فَخِذَيْهِ، وَقَالَ: يَا مُحَمَّدُ أَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِسْلَامِ. فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه و سلم الْإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إنْ اسْتَطَعْت إلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا. قَالَ: صَدَقْت . فَعَجِبْنَا لَهُ يَسْأَلُهُ وَيُصَدِّقُهُ! قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِيمَانِ. قَالَ: أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاَللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ، وَتُؤْمِنَ بِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ. قَالَ: صَدَقْت. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ الْإِحْسَانِ. قَالَ: أَنْ تَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ كَأَنَّك تَرَاهُ، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ تَرَاهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَرَاك. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ السَّاعَةِ. قَالَ: مَا الْمَسْئُولُ عَنْهَا بِأَعْلَمَ مِنْ السَّائِلِ. قَالَ: فَأَخْبِرْنِي عَنْ أَمَارَاتِهَا؟ قَالَ: أَنْ تَلِدَ الْأَمَةُ رَبَّتَهَا، وَأَنْ تَرَى الْحُفَاةَ الْعُرَاةَ الْعَالَةَ رِعَاءَ الشَّاءِ يَتَطَاوَلُونَ فِي الْبُنْيَانِ. ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَ، فَلَبِثْتُ مَلِيًّا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا عُمَرُ أَتَدْرِي مَنْ السَّائِلُ؟. ‫‬قُلْتُ: اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ. قَالَ: فَإِنَّهُ جِبْرِيلُ أَتَاكُمْ يُعَلِّمُكُمْ دِينَكُمْ ". [رَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ] .

عَنْ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبِي حَفْصٍ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: " إنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا أَوْ امْرَأَةٍ يَنْكِحُهَا فَهِجْرَتُهُ إلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إلَيْهِ". رَوَاهُ إِمَامَا الْمُحَدِّثِينَ

description:
അൽ ബഖറ | Part 98 | ആയ: 208-210
|| സമഗ്ര ഇസ്‌ലാം | പിശാചിന്റെ ശത്രുത ||
______________________________
EPISODE 104
BAQARA- PART 98

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي السِّلْمِ كَافَّةً وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ ۚ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ (208)
فَإِن زَلَلْتُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (209)
هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي ظُلَلٍ مِّنَ الْغَمَامِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ۚ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ (210)

description:
അൽ ബഖറ | Part 97 | ആയ: 204-207
|| വാക്‌സാമര്‍ഥ്യം കൈമുതലാക്കിയ കപടരും അവരുണ്ടാക്കുന്ന ദുരന്തങ്ങളും | ദൈവഹിതത്തിനായി ജീവാര്‍പ്പണം നടത്തുന്ന വിശ്വാസികളും ||
______________________________
EPISODE 103
BAQARA- PART 97

وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يُعجِبُكَ قَولُهُ فِي الحَياةِ الدُّنيا وَيُشهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلىٰ ما في قَلبِهِ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الخِصامِ (204)
وَإِذا تَوَلّىٰ سَعىٰ فِي الأَرضِ لِيُفسِدَ فيها وَيُهلِكَ الحَرثَ وَالنَّسلَ ۗ وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الفَسادَ (205)
وَإِذا قيلَ لَهُ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ أَخَذَتهُ العِزَّةُ بِالإِثمِ ۚ فَحَسبُهُ جَهَنَّمُ ۚ وَلَبِئسَ المِهادُ (206)
وَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَشري نَفسَهُ ابتِغاءَ مَرضاتِ اللَّهِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ رَءوفٌ بِالعِبادِ (207)

BAQARA- PART 96

فَإِذا قَضَيتُم مَناسِكَكُم فَاذكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكرِكُم آباءَكُم أَو أَشَدَّ ذِكرًا ۗ فَمِنَ النّاسِ مَن يَقولُ رَبَّنا آتِنا فِي الدُّنيا وَما لَهُ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِن خَلاقٍ- 200
وَمِنهُم مَن يَقولُ رَبَّنا آتِنا فِي الدُّنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنا عَذابَ النّارِ- 201

الحَجُّ أَشهُرٌ مَعلوماتٌ ۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فيهِنَّ الحَجَّ فَلا رَفَثَ وَلا فُسوقَ وَلا جِدالَ فِي الحَجِّ ۗ وَما تَفعَلوا مِن خَيرٍ يَعلَمهُ اللَّهُ ۗ وَتَزَوَّدوا فَإِنَّ خَيرَ الزّادِ التَّقوىٰ ۚ وَاتَّقونِ يا أُولِي الأَلبابِ -- 197

EPISODE 98
BAQARA- PART 92

title: Don’t Let Your Desires Replace Allah | Khutbah By Nouman Ali Khan
description:
There is a point where a person is no longer just following their desires. They begin worshiping them.

The Quran describes someone who once had the right idea of Allah, the right words, the right religious language and maybe even the right outward practices. But somewhere along the way, Allah was pushed out of the center and their feelings took His place. What they want, what they feel, what hurt them, what offended them and what their ego demands becomes the new authority.

That is why knowledge alone does not save a person in this state. You can show them the evidence. You can remind them of an ayah. You can make the truth as clear as day and it still makes no difference because the problem was never a lack of information. The problem is that their feelings have become too sacred to question.

The Quran then paints a terrifying picture: hearing sealed, heart sealed and sight covered. A person can hear the most powerful reminder and not hear it. They can see the damage they are causing and not stop. They can run toward their own destruction while still insisting they are right because every warning has to pass through the god of their feelings first.

This is how desire starts wearing a religious mask. A person can quote Quran, say Alhamdulillah, use Islamic language and still be using religion to decorate what their ego already decided.

And the warning goes both ways. We have to protect ourselves from becoming this person by constantly returning to what Allah actually says, not what we wish He said. But we also have to remember that some people are not ours to fix. When a person reaches a point where only Allah can turn them back, you stop destroying yourself trying to guide what Allah has not placed in your hands.

May Allah protect us from worshiping our own feelings while thinking we are still worshiping Him.

title: The Bias You Don't Admit To | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
Allah describes something happening deep inside every one of us, inside me, inside you: don't end up chasing empty feelings that keep you from being fair. The trap is subtle. Your feelings whisper that this person deserves less, because of what they said, because of how they treated you, so surely they shouldn't get as much as the other.

Picture a father who loves one son and is quietly annoyed with the other. Inheritance time comes, and the feeling gets in the way. This one used to massage my feet as a teenager. That one talked back to me. So one son gets the BMW, and the other gets the 1987 Hyundai, and the father tells himself it's fine, they both got a car.

That's exactly what Allah is warning against. Your feelings cannot get in the way of being fair. They cannot be the reason you tilt one way or the other. Justice means giving people their right even when your heart is pulling you somewhere else.

title: The Real Way Out of Trauma | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
Western psychology puts you at the center of the universe, so it tells you your healing has to come from within. That's exactly why the trauma keeps returning. The Quran points somewhere else entirely. Allah is the most important entity, which means your healing comes from outside you, from Allah.

So you won't find it at a Bali vacation. You won't undo your jealousy on a hike, or get over a breakup on a healing journey, or move past a conviction with an ocean sounds app. Those things might calm you, they might take your mind off it for a while, and that's fine. But if you really want to move on without guilt, without shame, without anger, without resentment, and lift the entire burden off your life, then you have to develop one relationship really well. When that one relationship with Allah becomes healthy, every other relationship can fall apart around you and you will still remain stable.

That is how the trauma actually lifts. It comes from the outside in. Western psychology can't take you there, because it insists nothing is greater than you. But once you turn to Allah first and let that light reach you, then you go inside out. It was always a two way street.

title: The Quran on Psychological Trauma | Nouman Ali Khan
description:
In a recent lecture that took place in Genk, Belgium, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan discusses Quran and human psychology and the emotion he focuses on is trauma. He opens with a warning: this is a heavy subject, and the way our culture talks about it may be doing us more harm than good.

Ustadh Nouman challenges the foundation of Western psychology, the idea popularized by Freud that we all start broken, that your family is a prison, and that healing means freeing yourself from everyone who hurt you. He contrasts this with the Quran, where the starting point of a human being is not brokenness at all. Then he walks through the prophets, Ibrahim, Nuh, Ayyub, Yunus, and Maryam, showing that their experiences were not small trauma but extreme trauma: rejection by family, years of effort with no results, illness in their own body, public humiliation, even obeying Allah leading to pain.

The turning point is where the Quran takes you next. Every other relationship in your life is unstable and can go either way, but the one relationship that never abandons you is with Allah, and that is where real healing begins, from the outside in. Your healing is not coming from inside you.

Do you feel helpless? Do you feel like you have no support? Do you feel alone, like nobody understands you? Like you keep trying to communicate, but the people on the other side just get angry and never grasp what you're actually saying, no matter how clearly you say it? These are some of the most common experiences in people's lives.

And here's the point: Allah already named all of it. Your trauma is in the Quran. The feelings you assume are just yours, the ones you'd only say out loud to a therapist, were described by Allah long before you ever felt them. That means you're not alone in it, and you're not the first to carry it.

title: Attention Is Their Oxygen
description:
Every community has a Samiri: someone charismatic and cunning enough to lead people away from what they know is right, often while everyone watches and argues about what to do. In this Story Night session, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan unpacks the final exchange between Musa (AS) and the Samiri from Surah Ta-Ha, focusing on the deceptively simple verdict Allah reveals: no contact, no engagement, no platform. The lesson is not merely historical. It is a direct Quranic strategy for households and communities navigating the pull of modern misleaders, online voices and local figures alike who thrive on being talked about, debated and exposed.

What makes this session so arresting is the practical clarity it offers. The answer is not a campaign against the Samiri in your life. It is withdrawal, irrelevance and a deliberate refusal to feed the cycle. Musa (AS) did not platform his enemy by making him a cause. He followed what Allah decreed in (20:97) and cut the connection entirely. That same wisdom is available to every Muslim household willing to apply it.

title: Why Allah Punished the Israelites Even After They Repented | Story Night: Breaking Free
description:
What happens when a whole nation witnesses miracle after miracle and still chooses shirk? In this Story Night session, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan unpacks one of the most haunting episodes in Quranic history: the aftermath of the golden calf, the rise and fall of the Samiri, and what Allah commanded next. The verse at the heart of this session is وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَـٰقَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِٱتِّخَاذِكُمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (2:54). Ustadh Nouman walks through how the Samiri built a cult by offering a transactional religion that mimicked prophetic authority, why Allah chose humiliation over execution as his punishment, and how the Israelites kept escalating in defiance even as Musa (AS) pleaded on their behalf. The conversation then moves to the shaking mountain, the 70 leaders, and Musa's (AS) remarkable du'aa that included his own people despite everything they had done. Every detail connects directly to patterns visible in our own time, from dream-influencers on social media to spiritual charlatans who charge in advance.

title: Allah is always present, always hearing and always seeing. But when we lose awareness of Him, fear b
description:
Allah is always present, always hearing and always seeing. But when we lose awareness of Him, fear becomes larger, anxiety becomes louder and the challenge begins to feel impossible.
The moment you bring Allah back into focus, your perspective changes. Courage returns. Your emotions begin to settle and the person threatening you no longer appears as powerful as they did before.
Remembering Allah does not remove every challenge. It gives you the strength and clarity to face it.

Taken from our YouTube video: "How To Deal With Tyrants In Your Life"

title: Enemies Within: Hypocrisy, Secret Meetings and Bad Intentions | Live Khutbah by Nouman Ali Khan
description:
During today's khutbah live from NAMCC in Austin, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan spoke about a concept Allah gives serious attention to in the Quran:

Najwa.

Najwa is not just a private conversation, it's the meeting after the meeting. The side conversation. The quiet circle where people say what they would not say openly, not to solve a problem, but to plant doubts, weaken trust, and pull others into confusion.

At the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Medina had sincere believers, hypocrites, and a large group in the middle who could be influenced either way. The hypocrites used najwa to create division from within the Muslim community. They sat in the same masjid, heard the same reminders, stood among the same Muslims, but behind the scenes they worked to poison people’s hearts.

That disease is still alive. It shows up in masjid boards, Muslim organizations, friend circles, WhatsApp groups, families, and workplaces. A decision is made, nobody speaks up clearly, and then the real "after-meeting" begins outside the room where people begin sharing their personal opinions. Slowly, people become suspicious, demotivated, and exhausted.

The Quran teaches us that communities don’t just need da‘wah outwardly, they need cleaning inwardly. Our homes, organizations, masajid, and circles need constant detox from the whispers, politics, and secret conversations that drain people’s sincerity and destroy good work from the inside.

title: What does it mean to truly hold onto what Allah has given you? In this Story Night session, Ustadh N
description: What does it mean to truly hold onto what Allah has given you? In this Story Night session, Ustadh Nouman Ali Khan draws from the story of Musa (AS) on the mountain to unpack one of the most grounding reminders in all of Surah Al-A'raf. When the mountain shattered at the manifestation of Allah, that same weight, Allah tells Musa (AS), now rests in His words and messages. Then the Ayah speaks directly: "[Allah] said, 'O Moses, I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful.'" (7:144). The lesson for every Muslim reading the Quran is built right into that address.

description:
Musa and Harun AS brought a genuine concern before Allah: Firaoun did not follow any rules. He could lie, threaten them, cross every boundary and use his power without restraint.

Some challenges in life feel exactly like this. You are trying to obey Allah while the other side appears willing to do anything to win.

The Quran does not dismiss this fear. It teaches us to bring it before Allah. Even when another person has no limits, they remain under the authority of the One who controls every outcome.

title: Mastering Hanafi Fiqh: A Structured Approach - Shaykh Faraz Rabbani & Dr. Talal Al-Azem
description:
The Hanafi school never left its students to find their own way through its vast literature. Over centuries, it developed a graded curriculum of relied-upon texts, carrying the student from foundational primers to the great works of later scholarship, such as Ibn Abidin's Radd al-Muhtar. This program brings together Dr. Talal Al-Azem, a scholar and researcher specializing in the history of fiqh and legal education, and Sheik Faraz Rabbani, a Hanafi jurist and founder of SeekersGuidance, to guide both our local and online community through this curriculum across three connected sessions. Attendees will come away knowing not only which books to read, but why they were written, in what order they are studied, and how to study them with real benefit — through sound preparation, presence of heart, and consistent review. For anyone who has picked up a fiqh text and felt unsure where to begin, or wondered how a lifetime of study is meant to unfold, this program offers a map: from the first primer to the frontier of specialization, and from correct information to godfearing practice.


Shaykh Faraz Rabbani:

Shaykh Faraz Rabbani is a recognized specialist scholar in the Islamic sciences, having studied under leading scholars from around the world. He is the Founder and Executive Director of SeekersGuidance. He spent ten years in traditional study, beginning in Damascus and continuing in Amman, Jordan. In Damascus, he studied with the late Shaykh Adib al-Kallas, renowned as the foremost theologian of his time, and with Shaykh Hassan al-Hindi, one of the leading Hanafi jurists of our era. Upon completing his studies, he returned to Canada in 2007 and founded SeekersGuidance, dedicated to making Islamic knowledge reliable, relevant, inspiring, and accessible, both online and on the ground. He is the author of Absolute Essentials of Islam: Faith, Prayer, and the Path of Salvation According to the Hanafi School (White Thread Press, 2004), and has been listed among the 500 Most Influential Muslims by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre since 2011.



Dr Talal Al-Azem:

Dr Talal Al-Azem is a teacher and researcher with interests in fiqh, Islamic education, and formations of the self in Islam. He studied the disciplines of Islamic learning in Syria and Turkey before completing a doctorate. He is the translator of Prayers of Occasions, a handbook of sunnah prayers, and the author of Rule-Formulation and Binding Precedent in the Madhhab-Law Tradition, a study of how rules were determined in the madhhabs.

description:
"I was really grateful to be able to find this program."

Zaynab came from the UK to Istanbul to study at university. Alongside her degree, she wanted to begin the Islamic sciences — but few programs were built to fit around a university timetable, and even fewer opened space for women in the evenings and on weekends.

She found that space at Tamkin, the SeekersGuidance in-person program at our Türkiye Centre in Istanbul. In this short testimonial, Zaynab shares what her first year looked like: teachers who supported her when she came in with no prior formal study, recorded classes that let her catch up around university, and a program that welcomed her at the level she was at.

"Prior to coming to Istanbul, I hadn't studied any Islamic sciences formally. But whenever I went to the teachers or asked for help, they were there to support me."

"I'd recommend this program to anyone — especially anyone in university, or women, or people from the West who haven't studied before. It caters to both people who've studied and those who haven't got as good a grasp of the sciences."

Tamkin is a structured in-person and online Islamic sciences program at the SeekersGuidance Türkiye Centre in Istanbul. title: Mastering the Core Islamic Sciences: Hadith
description:
Hadith science sits at the very heart of the Islamic intellectual tradition — yet its place within the broader map of Islamic disciplines has always been contested. In this seminar, Shaykh Issam Eido — a traditionally trained muḥaddith and academic scholar — guides participants through the architecture of the discipline: what it is, how it relates to kalām and uṣūl al-fiqh, and what its study actually demands. Drawing on decades of traditional training under masters such as Shaykh Nūr al-Dīn ʿItr and on his doctoral research into the criteria of early hadith critics, Shaykh Issam offers a rare synthesis of transmitted and analytical learning. Whether you are a student mapping your path through the Islamic sciences or a practitioner seeking to ground your knowledge more securely, this seminar provides an indispensable orientation.



With Shaykh Issam Eido:

Shaykh Issam Eido is Assistant Professor of the Practice of Religious Studies and Director of Undergraduate Studies in the Department of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University. He previously served as Visiting Professor of Islamic Studies and Arabic at the University of Chicago Divinity School and as a Research Fellow in the Program in Islamic Law at Harvard University. Prior to the Syrian uprising, he lectured in the Department of Qurʾān and Ḥadīth Studies at the University of Damascus. His doctoral dissertation, Early Ḥadīth Scholars and Their Criteria of Ḥadīth Criticism, presented a new analytical framework for understanding how classical scholars accepted or rejected traditions attributed to the Prophet. Shaykh Issam is among the foremost students of the late muḥaddith Shaykh Nūr al-Dīn ʿItr, and holds traditional ijāzas from Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Kurdī, Shaykh Muḥammad ʿAwwāma, Shaykh ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāghūrī, Shaykh Maḥmūd Maṣrī, and Shaykh Mahdī Khiḍr.



And Dr Talal Al-Azem:

Dr Talal Al-Azem is a teacher and researcher with interests especially in fiqh, Islamic education, and formations of the self in Islam. He studied the disciplines of Islamic learning in Syria and Turkey before completing a doctorate. He is the translator of Prayers of Occasions, a handbook of sunnah prayers, and the author of Rule-Formulation and Binding Precedent in the Madhhab-Law Tradition, a study of how rules were determined in the madhhabs.

title: Make Me Light: Wudu, Salah, and the Prophet's Dua — Shaykh Bassem Itani
description:
In this nasiha from the SeekersGuidance Türkiye Summer Intensive, Shaykh Bassem Itani reflects on a light that is anything but abstract.

Allah Most High asks: "Is he who was dead, and We gave him life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people, like one who is in utter darkness, unable to emerge from it?" [Quran 6:122]

This light, the Shaykh explains, begins in the ablution (wudu), walks with us to the mosque, and is completed in the prayer (salah). He calls us to carry the Prophet's own dua (Allah bless him and give him peace): "Allah, place light in my heart, my sight, my hearing, my tongue — and make me light." [Bukhari]

Carry this dua, and you join a chain of light stretching back to the Prophet himself. Make it part of your day.
